dedupe_keys.name: maryland food system map archive about 500 food system layers 2012 to 2023

description: This archive preserves the data behind the Maryland Food System Map, a free web mapping application run by the Johns Hopkins Center for a Livable Future from 2012 to 2023. The application combined data on the food system, public health and the environment so that users could explore geographic patterns, make their own maps and download data. It grew from 30 indicators to more than 400 layers, and the retired project deposited about 500 geospatial layers, the application code and documentation, including when and where each layer was obtained, in the Johns Hopkins Research Data Repository in 2023. Layers cover food retail such as supermarkets and corner stores, farms and farmers' markets, food assistance, health outcomes and demographics. Coverage is Maryland, mostly at point, census tract or county level. The archive is free to download from the repository; the DataCite record states no licence and the repository blocked automated access from the cloud. Caveats: the data are frozen at 2023 or earlier, sources and dates differ by layer, and the application itself is retired. Simulation uses: food access and food supply network inputs for Maryland and a template for state food system data. Related records: the Baltimore food system resilience planning study (case_study-baltimore-food-system-resilience-planning) works on the same region.
